entries.gloss_en: she bore, gave birth to (a child)
entries.notes: Form I fem. 3sg. past; ولَّد (form II) = act as midwife. In context Saadia uses ولدت consistently for birth of named figures.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ولد (wld): 'She brought forth a child; She bore a child' — waladatu, inf. n. wilādah and walādah.

entries.gloss_en: twisted linen thread; fine twisted yarn
entries.notes: Passive participle of شَزَرَ 'to twist'; used in Tabernacle weaving contexts (Ex 26:1) parallel to Hebrew שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר. Blau attests شزر = 'to twist' (citing Ibn Janāḥ).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شزر: $zr — to twist (thread); blau s.v. شزر (שזו): 'to twist'.

entries.gloss_en: dye; dyestuff (usually crimson dye)
entries.notes: صِبْغ (sibġ) = dye; in Saadia consistently as צבג' קרמז 'crimson dye' = תולעת שני. Lane: Sabagahu = 'he dyed it'. Blau: صبغ 'to be dyed / nrṭb'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صبغ (Sbg): 'He dyed it … a garment or piece of cloth'; blau s.v. صبغ (צבג): 'to be dyed / נצבע'.

entries.gloss_en: army, military force, troops
entries.notes: In Saadia גישה / גיוש = جَيْش 'army'. Lane: jy$ — 'assembled, armies, or military forces'. The form לגיושהם = لِجُيُوشِهِم 'for/in their armies'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. جيش (jy$): 'He collected, or assembled, an army, or a military force'; jayo$N = army.

entries.gloss_en: your localities, settlements, dwelling-places
entries.notes: Plural of مَحَلّ (maḥall) 'a place of abode, settlement' + 2ms suffix -ka; Lane: maHal~N = 'A place where a person or party alights … a place of alighting, or abode, or settlement'; pl. maḥāll. Saadia uses it for the localities/gates of Dt 12:17 etc.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حل (Hl): maHal~N … 'a place of alighting, or abode, or settlement … pl. maHaAl~u'.

entries.gloss_en: the right (side), right-hand
entries.notes: Fem. elative/superlative form of يَمِين; الْيُمْنَى = the right side. Lane: 'Alyamiynu * The location that is on the right.' Saadia: יד אלימני / אד'ן אלימני = right hand / right ear.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. يمن (ymn): 'Alyamiynu * The location that is on the right'.

entries.gloss_en: his heart (as seat of will, courage, emotion)
entries.notes: قَلْب (qalb) + 3ms suffix -hu. Lane: qalobN * = 'The heart'. Saadia: פשכך קלבה = 'his heart doubted/hesitated'; לא ירתפע קלבה = 'his heart shall not be lifted up'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قلب (qlb): 'qalobN * The heart; syn. fuw^aAdN'.

entries.gloss_en: or (disjunctive, in questions: 'which of the two?')
entries.notes: Disjunctive interrogative conjunction. Lane: 'A^amo * is a conjunction … It denotes interrogation … corresponding to the interrogative A^a … meaning A^aY~ … which of them two.' Distinct from أَوْ (aw). In Saadia: אהו שדיד אם מסתרכ'י = 'Is it strong, or lax?'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أم (Am): 'A^amo * is a conjunction … It denotes interrogation … meaning A^aY~: which of the two?'

entries.gloss_en: your servants, your slaves (collective honorific)
entries.notes: عَبِيد = pl. of عَبْد 'slave, servant'; + 2ms -ka. Used in Saadia as a self-referential honorific plural when addressing a superior (Moses, God). Lane: 'He was, or became, a slave, or in a state of slavery'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عبد (Ebd): slave/servant — Eabada, EibaAdapN; EabiydN = slave; pl. EabiydN.

entries.gloss_en: he does, performs, carries out (a deed or act)
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms; EamalaN = 'He worked, or wrought; he did, acted, or performed'. Saadia uses יעמל for 'shall do' (vow text) and for manual work.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عمل (Eml): 'Eamila … aor. Eamala, inf. n. EamalN, He worked, or wrought … he did, acted, or performed'.

entries.gloss_en: your companion, fellow, neighbor
entries.notes: صَاحِب (ṣāḥib) + 2ms -ka = 'your companion/associate'. Lane: SHb 1 = 'He associated, kept company, or consorted, with him … SAHibN = companion, associate, comrade, fellow, friend'. Blau attests a JA sense 'husband' (influenced by Heb. בעל) — but Saadia uses it in the standard classical sense of 'companion/neighbor'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صحب (SHb): 'SaHibahu … He associated, kept company, or consorted, with him … companion, associate, comrade, fellow, friend'.

entries.gloss_en: he released, let go, set free
entries.notes: Form IV of طَلَقَ. Lane: 'A^aTolaqa … He let go the captive; and set him free; he loosed the bond of the captive, and let him go'. In Gen 8:7 = שלח הערב; Gen 8:8 = שלח הת יונה.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. طلق (Tlq) form 4: 'ATlq AlA^asiyra … He let go the captive; and set him free; he loosed the bond'.

entries.gloss_en: the interior, inside, inner cavity (of body or structure)
entries.gloss_he: הפנים, חלל הפנים (של גוף או מבנה)
entries.notes: Lane: jawofN = 'It reached his jawof [or inside, or interior]'. In Saadia: אלשחם אלמג'טי אלגוף = 'the fat covering the cavity/interior', and אלמהג אלאוסט פי גוף אלתכ'אתג = 'the bar through the interior of the planks'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. جوف (jwf): 'jaAfatohu … jawofN [or inside, or interior, &c.]'; inf. n. jawofN = 'It reached his jawof'.

entries.gloss_en: their nobleman, chieftain, leader
entries.notes: شَرِيف (šarīf) = 'high, noble, possessing glory, honour, or nobility … the pl. is A^a$oraAfN and $urafaA^'. Saadia uses ושריפהם for the tribal chief named after each camp unit (Num 2).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شرف ($rf): '$ariyfN * High, elevated, exalted, or eminent … possessing glory, honour, dignity, or nobility; pl. A^a$oraAfN and $urafaA^'.

entries.gloss_en: and she named him, called him by the name
entries.notes: Form II 3fs past of سَمَّى (sm~Y) + 3ms suffix; Lane: 'sm~Y … He named him, or called him, Such a one; … he made [such] to be his name, his proper name.' In Saadia: ואסמתה ראובן = 'and she named him Reuben'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. سمو (smw) form II: 'sm~Y … teshdeed … He named him, or called him, Such a one'.

entries.gloss_en: gift, present sent as an act of courtesy or honor
entries.notes: Lane: 'hadiy~apN * [n. un.] A present; i.e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour'. In Gen 32:19: הד'א הדייה מבעות'ה לסיידי = 'this is a gift sent to my lord'. In Gen 4:3: הדייה ללה = 'an offering to God'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. هدي (hdy): 'hadiy~apN * A present; i.e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour'.

entries.gloss_en: he crossed over, passed across (a river, border)
entries.notes: Form I: Eabara = 'He passed, went, or crossed, over it … namely a river'. Also used as noun עבר = عِبْر 'the side/bank (of the Jordan)': Lane cites EiborN = 'the side of a river'. In Num 32 Saadia alternates verb and noun senses.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عبر (Ebr): 'Eabara bihi … He passed … from one side thereof to the other … a river'; also EiborN 'the side' of a river.

entries.gloss_en: a curtain panel, an oblong strip of cloth
entries.notes: Lane: '$aq~apN * primarily signifies The half of a garment … applied to an oblong piece; syn. sabiybapN musotaTiylapN … pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN.' In Ex 26:2 Saadia: כל שקה = 'each curtain strip'. Plural is שקאק = شِقَاق.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شق ($qq): '$aq~apN * primarily the half of a garment … an oblong piece … pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN'.

entries.gloss_en: the well (water-well)
entries.notes: بِئْر (bi'r) is classical Arabic for well (masc. in classical, often fem.); Lisan: 'البِئْرُ: القَلِيبُ، أُنثى، والجمع أَبْآرٌ'. Lane references biy^orN throughout. Saadia: אגמע אלקום ... אעטיהם מאא = 'assemble the people … I will give them water' (Num 21:16–18).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. بأر: 'البِئْرُ: القَلِيبُ، أُنثى، والجمع أَبْآرٌ'; lane passim biy^orN 'A well'.

entries.gloss_en: the two tablets (stone), dual construct
entries.notes: لَوْح (lawḥ) = 'That [meaning a tablet] upon which one writes'. Dual لَوْحَيْ (lawḥay). Lane: 'lawoHN … That [a tablet] upon which one writes; katabonaA lahu fiY AlA^alowaAHi [We wrote … upon the tablets]'. Saadia: נחת לוחי גוהר = 'I hewed tablets of stone'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. لوح (lwH): 'lawoHN … That upon which one writes … (Kur vii. 142) AlA^alowaAHi [tablets]'.

entries.gloss_en: day of rest, holiday, cessation from work
entries.notes: Blau attests عُطْلَة = 'holiday, free day / יום פגרה' with explicit citation from Saadia's Tafsir on Lev 26:34. Lane has EuTolapN = 'the state of being without work, or occupation' but does not yield 'rest day'. Blau is the primary reference for the Saadia-specific sense.
entries._grounding: blau s.v. عطلة (עטלה): 'holiday, free day / יום פגרה'; citing Saadia Tafsir Lev (וס"ג לויקרא).

entries.gloss_en: a people, nation, tribe
entries.notes: Lane: '$aEobN * … A great number of people; … a tribe, or nation'. In Saadia consistently = עם/לאום: שעב מקדס ללה = 'a holy nation to God'; שעב כלבו יקום = 'a people, as a lion, shall rise'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شعب ($Eb): '$aEobN * A great number of people … a tribe or nation'.

entries.gloss_en: Gershon (son of Levi, head of Levitical clan)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name, Hebrew גֵּרְשׁוֹן, transliterated into Judeo-Arabic. No Arabic root. Appears throughout Num as the tribe responsible for carrying Tabernacle coverings.
entries._grounding: proper noun — Hebrew biblical name גֵּרְשׁוֹן, JA transliteration.

entries.gloss_en: he enters, comes into (service, assembly)
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms of دَخَلَ (dakala). Standard classical Arabic. Lane: dakala = 'He entered; he came, or went, in, or into'. Saadia: ידכל לאלגיש = 'he enters into the army/service'; לא ידכל מפדוג' = 'an injured person shall not enter'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. دخل (dxl): 'daxala … He entered; he came, or went, in, or into'.

entries.gloss_en: for war, for battle, for combat
entries.notes: لِـ + الْحَرْب: Lane: 'HarobN Hrb War, battle, fight, or conflict; contr. of silomN'. In Saadia: לאלחרב = 'to/for battle' (Num 21:33; 32:27).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حرب (Hrb): 'HarobN Hrb War, battle, fight, or conflict; contr. of silomN'.

entries.gloss_en: springs (of water); also: eyes (dual/pl.)
entries.notes: Plural of عَيْن (ʿayn) = eye / spring of water. Lane: 'AlEayonu signifies The eye'; and 'maA^N maEiynN … Water of which one has reached the springs or sources'. Saadia uses עיון אלג'מר = 'the springs of the great deep' (Gen 7:11); also עיון אלגמאעה = 'inadvertence of the congregation' (lit. 'eyes = awareness').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عين (Eyn): 'AlEayonu signifies The eye … pl. EuyuwnN (عيون)'; spring of water sense also attested.

entries.gloss_en: strong, mighty, severe, harsh
entries.notes: Fem. form of شَدِيد (šadīd). Lane: '$adiydN * strong, powerful, mighty'. In Saadia: יד שדידה = 'a mighty hand'; שדידה is the fem. agreeing with יد (hand) or referring to a force.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شدد ($dd): '$adiydN * strong, powerful, mighty … بَيِّنُ الشِّدَّةِ'; lisan s.v. شدد: 'شيء شَدِيدٌ: مُشتَدٌّ قَوِيٌّ'.

entries.gloss_en: your land, your soil, your ground
entries.notes: أَرْض (arḍ) + 2ms -ka. Lane: 'A^aroDN * The earth … a land, or country'. The ḍ is represented by ץ' (with apostrophe for Arabic letter ض). In Saadia: אמץ' מן ארצ'ך = 'depart from your land' (Gen 12:1).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أرض (A^rD): 'A^aroDN * The earth; a land, or country; a region; a tract'.

entries.gloss_en: Hagar (Egyptian maidservant of Sarah, mother of Ishmael)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name. Arabic هَاجَر (Hājar) is the standard Arabic form of Hebrew הָגָר. Lane does not have a dedicated entry for this name. Appears throughout Gen 16 in Saadia.
entries._grounding: proper noun — biblical Hebrew הָגָר; Arabic هَاجَر is the standard Arabic biblical form.

entries.gloss_en: a full measure of; enough to fill
entries.notes: مِلْء (mil') = 'the filling of a vessel; the amount that fills'. Lisan: 'مَلأَ الشيءَ يَمْلَؤُه مَلأً' = 'He filled the thing'. In Saadia: מל ביתה פצ'ה וד'הב = 'the full of his house of silver and gold' (Num 22:18); מל אלמכ'אזין = 'filling the granaries' (Gen 41:47).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. ملأ: 'مَلأَ الشيءَ يَمْلَؤُه مَلأً … مِلْء = the filling / amount that fills'.

entries.gloss_en: a staff, rod, stick
entries.notes: عَصًا (ʿaṣā), originally عَصَوٌ. Lane: 'EaSFA * i.q. EuwdN [a staff, or stick, or rod]'. In Saadia Num 17: עצא עצא לכל בית אב = 'a staff for each ancestral house'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عصو (ESw): 'EaSFA * i.q. EuwdN [as meaning A staff, or stick, or rod]'.

entries.gloss_en: craft, trade, skilled work, handiwork
entries.notes: Lane: 'SinaAEapN … the Hirofap [i.e. craft or handicraft, or a trade] … any habitual work or occupation'. In Saadia: ליעמל צנאעה פי כ'בא = 'to perform service in the Tent of Meeting'; לא תצנע פיה צנאעה = 'do not perform work in it'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صنع (SnE): 'SinaAEapN … craft or handicraft, or a trade … any habitual work or occupation'.

entries.gloss_en: Shem (eldest son of Noah, ancestor of Semitic peoples)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name. Arabic سَام (Sām) = Hebrew שֵׁם. Standard transliteration in Islamic/JA tradition. Appears in Saadia's Gen 10 as the ancestor of the Semitic nations.
entries._grounding: proper noun — Hebrew שֵׁם; Arabic سَام is the standard Arabic biblical/Quranic form.

entries.gloss_en: with stones, by stoning
entries.notes: بِـ + الْحِجَارَة = 'with stones'. Lane: HajarN / HijaArapN = 'A stone; pl. HijaArapN'. Saadia: ירגמוהמא באלחגארה = 'they shall stone them with stones'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حجر (Hjr): 'HajarN … A stone; pl. HijaArapN'.

entries.gloss_en: he rises, stands up; fulfills, carries out
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms of قَامَ. Lane: 'qaAma … He rose, i.e. from sitting or reclining'. Saadia uses it in two senses: (a) physical 'he shall rise' (Num 23:24), (b) metaphorical 'carries out / fulfills' (Num 23:19: 'does he speak and not carry it out?').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قوم (qwm): 'qaAma … He rose, i.e. from sitting or reclining; He stood up'.

entries.gloss_en: the (dining) table set with food
entries.notes: Lane: 'maAy^idapN * A table with food upon it; without food upon it, a table is not thus called, but is called xiwaAnN'. Saadia uses it for the Tabernacle shewbread table (Ex 25:23; Num 3:31).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ميد (myd): 'maAy^idapN * A table with food upon it'.

entries.gloss_en: those who dwell, reside, are settled (in a place)
entries.notes: Active participle (form IV) of أَقَامَ 'to reside, settle'; pl. مُقِيمِينَ. Lane: 'muqiymN * Lasting; continuing … resident'. Saadia: אלקום אלמקימין פיה = 'the people who reside in it'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قوم (qwm): 'muqiymN * Lasting, continuing … resident'; masc. pl. muqiymuwna/muqiymiynaA.

entries.gloss_en: nakedness, pudenda (as object of sexual prohibition)
entries.notes: سَوْأَة (saw'a) = pudendum, nakedness. Lisan: 'السَّوْأَةُ: الفَرْجُ … فالسَّوْأَةُ كلُّ عَمَلٍ وأَمْرٍ شائن'. Used in Saadia as the JA equivalent of Hebrew עֶרְוָה throughout Lev 18 incest prohibitions. Blau does not have a clear separate entry for saw'a in this sense.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. سوأ: 'السَّوْأَةُ: الفَرْجُ. الليث: السَّوْأَةُ: فَرْج الرَّجل والمرأَة. قال اللّه تعالى: بَدَتْ لهما سَوْآتُهما'.

entries.gloss_en: then he returned, went back
entries.notes: فَ (then/so) + رَجَعَ (he returned). Lane: 'rajaEa … He returned; he went, or came, back'. The פ- prefix = Arabic فـ 'so, then'. Saadia: פרגע הרון אלי' מוסי = 'then Aaron returned to Moses'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. رجع (rjE): 'rajaEa … He returned; he went, or came, back … he reverted; contr. of *ahaba'.
